packages.note: ElevenLabs is the only paid service you may call, through tools/audio/eleven_sfx.py: ceiling 20000 credits for this package (the M6 policy stop is 30000; AUDIO's voices used part of it, read the ledger first). Never print, log or write the key. Each job's MP3s go into a new empty folder and reach ffmpeg as path arguments. You can't hear: choose by measured features, and leave the judgement to Game-boy's audition room. Measured (AUDIO): ElevenLabs costs 10 credits a second, not 40 (eleven_policy.json credits_per_second); about 1650 of the 30000 stop are spent, so three candidates per clip fit easily. The counter lags a call by 30-60 s: use the tool as it is (its settle lines) and --reconcile after a killed run. Beds loop because the director forces loop_mode in code; never rely on an .import loop flag. Voices are RMS -16 dBFS while the hit stack is peak-normalised at -1 dBFS: rebalance grunt_db, windup_db, ko_db and the hit stack's dB tunables so a voice doesn't sit over a hit. The weapon pools are weapon_pipe_hit and weapon_bike_chain_hit (WEAPONS sets impact_sfx pipe and bike_chain). empty_slots starts at 16 (barriers 6, weapons 6, stings 2, beds 2) and your done-when is 0; generated_sfx goes to 0 except music_loop (allowed, D25).
